evals.prompt: Create a VISION.md for this new CLI project. It overlaps with several package managers and sync tools.
evals.expected_output: A durable decision-framework vision doc grounded in project identity, competitor scan, fatal gaps, and delegate→contribute→absorb verdicts.
expectations: Reads project identity sources such as README, AGENTS, existing VISION, package metadata, and TASKS before asking new questions
Runs a broad market scan across GitHub, package ecosystems, alternatives links, and awesome lists
Classifies competitors by overlap percentage and gives direct competitors explicit delegate/contribute/keep-separate verdicts
Defines permanent scope as fatal gaps the ecosystem does not cover
Writes concise decision-framework sections and adds TASKS.md entries for delegate/contribute verdicts

evals.prompt: The market scan found two tools that cover everything except one tiny convenience feature. Write the vision anyway.
evals.expected_output: An honest halt that surfaces the possibility the project should dissolve into upstream contributions.
expectations: Checks whether the fatal-gap list has zero or one durable item
Does not invent permanent scope to justify the project
Tells the user the project may not need to exist separately
Asks whether to continue writing a vision or reconsider the reason to exist
Treats dissolution into upstream contributions as a valid outcome

evals.prompt: Review our architecture and give a one-time strategic analysis, but do not rewrite the durable vision doc.
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware response that routes one-shot architecture analysis to strategic-review rather than write-vision.
expectations: Distinguishes durable vision authoring from one-shot strategic analysis
Does not rewrite VISION.md when the user asked only for a review artifact
Recommends strategic-review for architecture fitness, pivot signals, and build/buy/kill analysis
Keeps write-vision for new docs or shifted strategic positioning
Avoids mixing code-level bug findings into a vision rewrite

evals.prompt: Write a vision document for a new CLI tool that helps developers manage environment variables across multiple deployment environments.
evals.expected_output: A docs/VISION.md that articulates the market niche, applies delegate-contribute-absorb to every competitor, defines permanent scope as ecosystem gaps, and includes decision framework and re-evaluation triggers.
expectations: Discovers at least 15-30 competitor tools using GitHub search, package ecosystem search, and awesome lists
Classifies each competitor by overlap percentage (80%+, 30-79%, <30%) and applies the 3-step test to direct competitors
For each 80%+ competitor, provides a specific verdict: Delegate (shell out to upstream), Contribute (file RFC/PR with 90-day window), or Keep separate (with documented reason)
Identifies fatal gaps (what no upstream tool covers) and halts if the list has zero or one item

Produces a vision doc with: problem statement, solution, primary user, core beliefs (including delegate-contribute-absorb), user stories, what we're building/not building, decision framework, success metrics, permanent scope list, and competitor verdicts table
Includes 4-8 concrete re-evaluation triggers (observable signals, not subjective judgment) that force reconsidering the strategy

evals.prompt: Our project's strategy has shifted. Rewrite the vision document to reflect that we're now focusing on enterprise features instead of open-source adoption.
evals.expected_output: An updated docs/VISION.md that reflects the new strategic direction, with updated competitor analysis, permanent scope redefinition, and re-evaluation triggers.
expectations: Reads the existing VISION.md and identifies what's changed (target user, market positioning, build/buy/kill decisions)
Re-evaluates competitors in the context of the new strategy (some may become less relevant, new ones may emerge)
Updates the permanent scope list to reflect enterprise-specific gaps (compliance, audit logging, multi-tenancy, etc.)
Revises the decision framework to accept/reject features based on enterprise fit rather than open-source adoption
Updates success metrics to measure enterprise adoption (paying customers, enterprise features shipped) instead of GitHub stars
Includes a 'Current Positioning' section explaining the enterprise-first posture with a reversal path if the strategy changes again

evals.prompt: I'm starting a new project and need a vision document that will guide all future feature decisions. The project is currently just me, so breaking changes are free.
evals.expected_output: A concise docs/VISION.md (200-300 lines) that clearly defines the project's niche, permanent scope, and decision framework, with explicit acknowledgment of single-user status and breaking-changes-free posture.
expectations: Establishes project identity: one-sentence problem, one-paragraph solution, one command/workflow, primary user (the author), current user count (1)
Discovers and classifies 15+ competitors, applying the 3-step test to each 80%+ overlap
Identifies fatal gaps that justify the project's existence (if none found, halts and recommends dissolving into upstream contributions)
Explicitly states 'Today's user base: 1 (the author). Breaking changes are free until user count grows past [threshold].'
Defines permanent scope as the fatal-gap list with one sentence per gap explaining why no upstream tool covers it
Includes a decision framework with Rule #1: 'Does this fit the permanent scope, or is it a delegation candidate?'
